title: Human Dependence on God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Human dependence on God means that people are not self-sustaining or self-ruling beings. Life, breath, strength, wisdom, provision, and purpose come from the Lord who made and upholds all things.
summary: Human dependence on God means that people are not self-sustaining or self-ruling beings. Life, breath, strength, wisdom, provision, and purpose come from the Lord who made and upholds all things.
christFocus: Jesus Christ lived in perfect dependence on the Father and teaches His people to trust God for life, provision, obedience, and salvation. Through Him, believers learn to stop pretending they can live apart from God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Human beings are dependent creatures. They receive life and breath from God and continue to exist only because He sustains them. Independence from God is an illusion created by pride and unbelief.

Scripture repeatedly exposes the limits of human control. People do not command tomorrow, supply their own life, or determine their own destiny. Even ordinary provision is a mercy from the Creator.

Jesus taught His followers not to be ruled by anxiety because the Father knows what they need. Dependence does not mean passivity; it means faithful obedience while trusting God rather than pretending to be God.

Sin twists dependence into pride, anxiety, self-reliance, and fear. The Gospel restores believers to childlike trust, teaching them to abide in Christ and receive grace for every step.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people carry burdens God never called them to carry as though everything depends on their control. Others boast as if their strength, plans, and success came from themselves. Dependence on God humbles pride and comforts anxiety.

This doctrine is especially precious for the weak, disabled, recovering, and weary. Human limitation is not proof that life is worthless. Every person already depends on God, and Christ meets His people in that dependence with sustaining grace.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Confess your dependence on God in prayer, planning, work, suffering, and obedience. Do not boast in your strength or despair over your weakness. Abide in Christ, ask for daily provision, receive limitations humbly, and trust the Father who knows what you need.
